text: The workflow begins with the Breast Cancer Image Dataset, which supplies data across two parallel training branches.
In the segmentation branch, raw ultrasonography images are first extracted from the dataset.
These raw images undergo preprocessing to standardize their input characteristics.
Spatial scaling is first applied to resize each image to uniform dimensions.
Pixel normalization is then performed to ensure consistent intensity distributions across the dataset.
Next, Simple Linear Iterative Clustering clusters pixels into superpixels to address non-linear artifacts.
The superpixel representations are fed into a modified U-Net architecture to perform semantic segmentation.
This completes the training phase, yielding the trained segmentation model.
In parallel, ground truth masked images and labels are routed into the classification branch.
A pre-trained VGG 16 backbone extracts high-level convolutional features from masked images.
Extracted features are processed through fully connected dense layers for tumor classification.
This training process establishes the finalized detection model.
Finally, both trained models are integrated to construct the end-to-end breast cancer detection pipelining framework.
